clue.text: Sailor most of all appearing as one late to the feast

parts.note: Jack, or Jack tar, is a traditional name for a sailor

indicators.note: most of a word means all but its final letter is kept

explanation.surface: A sailor seems to be the last guest arriving at a banquet, a figure of fun at most.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the last letter of ALL, leaving AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Jackals are scavengers that arrive at a kill after the hunters have eaten, so they come late to the feast.

clue.text: Marine debris not including missile or plane

indicators.note: not including says one piece is removed from the other

parts.note: jetsam is cargo thrown overboard that floats or washes ashore
a SAM is a surface-to-air missile

explanation.surface: Floating rubbish in the sea is said to exclude rockets and aircraft, like a salvage inventory.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking SAM out of JETSAM leaves the answer; 'or' joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A jet is a jet-propelled aircraft, an everyday synonym for an aeroplane.

clue.text: Guarantee remedy requires swapping Nos. 1 & 3 in order

indicators.note: the first and third letters of the word for remedy change places

parts.note: to remedy a fault is to rectify it

explanation.surface: Reads like an instruction for a bureaucratic fix: a guarantee needs items one and three reordered.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the R and C of RECTIFY turns REC into CER.
explanation.definitionFit: To certify something is to vouch for it formally, a verb synonym of guarantee.

clue.text: Strange article concealing location of golfball?

indicators.note: concealing means the article wraps round the other piece

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
in golf the lie is where the ball comes to rest

explanation.surface: An odd item hides where a golf ball has ended up, like a lost-ball mystery on the course.
explanation.definitionFit: Alien as an adjective means foreign or unfamiliar, a synonym of strange.

clue.text: Damage one area in seas

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or damage
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Something harmful happening to a single region of the oceans, like an environmental news item.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition hides a lunar sense: the dark plains of the Moon were named as if they were water.
explanation.definitionFit: Maria (plural of mare) are the lunar 'seas', the dark basaltic plains on the Moon's surface.

clue.text: Possibly lead group to adopt new way of thinking

indicators.note: to adopt means to take something in, so a letter goes inside

parts.note: lead is one example of a metal, hence possibly
a set is a group of things

explanation.surface: Suggests a leader urging their team to embrace fresh thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' reads as leading people, but it is the heavy element; 'to adopt' takes the new letter in.
explanation.definitionFit: A mental set is a fixed habitual approach to problems, a psychology term for a mindset.

clue.text: Composer's uppity nipper ditching contralto and embracing soprano

indicators.note: embracing means a letter is taken inside
ditching means a letter is thrown out
uppity in a down clue means the word is read upwards, from the bottom

parts.note: an incisor is a front tooth that nips
C abbreviates contralto in vocal scores

explanation.surface: A cheeky child drops one singer and takes up another, as though in a choir dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uppity' turns INCISOR into ROSICNI; 'ditching' removes C, and S goes in. 'Composer's' is 'Composer is'. 'nipper' suggests a child but is a tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: Gioachino Rossini was the Italian who wrote The Barber of Seville and William Tell.

clue.text: Girl embraced by two Italians?

indicators.note: embraced by says the girl sits inside the letters that follow

parts.note: the word Italian written twice in a row, one for each Italian

explanation.surface: A young woman being hugged by a pair of Italian men.
explanation.walkthrough: Write ITALIAN twice, ITALIANITALIAN, and the name sits across the join.
explanation.definitionFit: Anita is a female given name, and crosswords freely use girl for any woman's name.

clue.text: Wordiest styles left out in redrafting musical

indicators.note: redrafting means the remaining letters are rewritten in a new order
out signals the letter is taken away

explanation.surface: An editor cutting a florid writing style while revising a stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop L from WORDIESTSTYLES, as 'out' says, and the remaining thirteen letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: West Side Story is the Bernstein and Sondheim stage show reworking Romeo and Juliet in New York.

clue.text: Both sides I included in bet regarding the leading players?

indicators.note: included in puts these letters inside the bet

parts.note: a stake is a sum wagered
right and left, R and L, are both sides

explanation.surface: A gambler hedges both ways on the top performers in some contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Both sides' gives right and left; 'included in' puts them, with I, inside the bet.
explanation.definitionFit: Starlike describes what resembles stars, and the stars of a show are its leading players; the question mark flags the stretch.

clue.text: Water monster is seen at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A sighting of a sea creature, as in a sailor's tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Nessie is the nickname of the Loch Ness Monster, a legendary creature said to live in a Scottish lake.

clue.text: Group heading off legal case

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a faction is a group within a larger body

explanation.surface: A group forestalling a lawsuit, like lobbyists heading off litigation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' reads as preventing, but it drops the F of FACTION.
explanation.definitionFit: An action is a lawsuit, a legal proceeding brought in court.

clue.text: Name for group in church?

indicators.note: in places the group inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CH abbreviates church, as on maps
a lot is a group or batch

explanation.surface: Asks for a collective noun for church people.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: the clergy are the group in church.
explanation.definitionFit: The cloth is an idiom for the clergy as a body, from the distinctive clerical dress.

clue.text: Tenor second with songs enshrining Northern noblewomen

indicators.note: enshrining means the songs hold a letter within them

parts.note: arias are operatic songs

explanation.surface: An opera tenor with songs celebrating aristocratic ladies of the north.
explanation.definitionFit: Tsarinas were Russian empresses or wives of tsars, women of the highest nobility.

clue.text: Theatre award never taken back by unknown

indicators.note: taken back means the word is turned round

parts.note: not is a near synonym of never
Y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A theatre prize never reclaimed by some anonymous figure.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tonys are the Antoinette Perry Awards for Broadway theatre.

clue.text: Fielders longing to catch team's opener? One offers little in the way of catching material

definitions.text: One offers little in the way of catching material

indicators.note: to catch means a letter is held inside

parts.note: slips are close catching fielders in cricket, beside the wicketkeeper
an itch is a longing

indicators.note: opener means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Cricket fielders eager for a dismissal of the batting side's first man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to catch' holds the team's first letter between fielders and longing. The definition plays on catching: the stitch picks up only a thread of fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip stitch is a sewing stitch that catches only a tiny amount of fabric so it stays nearly invisible.

clue.text: The stuff of explosives? Steel part buckled

indicators.note: buckled means bent out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A steel component twisted, perhaps by a blast.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltpetre, potassium nitrate, is the oxidising ingredient of gunpowder.

clue.text: Some ranch in Oregon producing cotton

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A farm in Oregon growing cotton.
explanation.definitionFit: Chino is a twilled cotton fabric, so the material is the cotton the clue mentions.

clue.text: Most perfectly formed — can you make me this, please?

indicators.note: the clue asks the solver to make the answer out of the words that follow, rearranging them

explanation.surface: A polite request for the most beautiful version of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Shapeliest is the superlative of shapely, meaning best proportioned in form.

clue.text: Old man taking university approach regarding religious texts

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father, the old man
a line is an approach or method

explanation.surface: A father going to university to study scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: Pauline means relating to St Paul, especially his New Testament epistles.

clue.text: Attack that's half-repulsed bearing little fruit

indicators.note: half of the word is driven back, so only its first two letters are turned round

parts.note: a raid is an attack

explanation.surface: An assault partly beaten off, yielding little reward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-repulsed' reverses RA to AR, leaving ID in place.
explanation.definitionFit: Arid land is dry and barren, producing few crops.

clue.text: A sense about soccer team being worried

indicators.note: about means the sense goes round the team

parts.note: nous is common sense
XI, eleven in Roman numerals, is a football side

explanation.surface: A feeling that a football side is nervous.
explanation.definitionFit: Anxious describes uneasy concern, a close synonym for worried.

clue.text: Prostitute to play idly with favoured person

parts.note: to strum is to play a guitar casually
a teacher's pet is a favoured person

explanation.surface: A sex worker fooling around with a favourite client.
explanation.definitionFit: Strumpet is an old-fashioned word for a woman who sells sex.

clue.text: Rows hard: vessel is to catch good fish

indicators.note: to catch means a letter is taken inside

parts.note: tiers are rows set one above another
H abbreviates hard, as on pencils
Noah's ark is a vessel

explanation.surface: A rower toiling while a boat sets out to land a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to catch' puts the good letter inside the rows; Noah's vessel ends the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiger shark is a large striped predatory species found in warm seas.

clue.text: Church worker to attack, carrying cross

indicators.note: carrying means holding a letter within

parts.note: to set on someone is to attack them
X is a cross

explanation.surface: A churchgoer going on the offensive armed with a crucifix.
explanation.definitionFit: A sexton is a church officer who looks after the building and churchyard.

clue.text: See 20
A key point about rear of carriage? Overlooking those getting on

indicators.note: about means the main point goes round a letter

parts.note: the gist is the essential point

indicators.note: rear of means the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A railway image: passengers boarding at the back of a carriage being missed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'those getting on' suggests passengers boarding but means older people.
explanation.definitionFit: An ageist attitude discriminates against or ignores the elderly, those advancing in years.

clue.text: Description of memory, sincere then variable, probed by academic

indicators.note: probed by means another piece is pushed inside

parts.note: real feelings are sincere ones
a don is a university teacher
Y is an algebraic variable

explanation.surface: Someone's genuine but changeable recollections being examined by a scholar.
explanation.definitionFit: Read-only memory in computing can be read but not rewritten.

clue.text: Stories giving away English and French royal symbol

indicators.note: giving away means a letter is lost

parts.note: lies are stories, falsehoods
E abbreviates English; that the three letters also sit in the word English is a coincidence

explanation.surface: Tales betraying Anglo-French royal emblems.
explanation.definitionFit: The lis is the fleur-de-lis, the lily emblem of French kings.

clue.text: Magistrate to change in attitude, retreating before end of case

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: to veer is to change direction or opinion

indicators.note: end of means the last letter

explanation.surface: A magistrate changing their stance and backing down before a case closes.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve was a local official in medieval England with judicial duties, a chief magistrate of a district.

clue.text: Peremptory commands when beset by stringed instruments

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded, so the word sits inside

parts.note: ukes are ukuleles
as means when

explanation.surface: Orders issued while surrounded by stringed instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: Ukases were edicts of the Russian tsar, hence any arbitrary decree.
